about.title: About Urban Heritage
about.subtitle: We are a passionate team dedicated to preserving and celebrating the architectural and cultural heritage of Massawa and the greater Red Sea region.
about.storyP1: Founded with a vision to protect and promote the rich cultural legacy of Massawa, Urban Heritage brings together historians, architects, and community advocates.
about.storyP2: Massawa, often called the "Pearl of the Red Sea," boasts a unique blend of Ottoman, Egyptian, and Italian colonial architecture dating back centuries. Our mission is to ensure these treasures are documented, preserved, and celebrated for generations to come.
about.storyP3: Through partnerships with local communities, international organizations, and academic institutions, we work tirelessly to maintain the integrity of historic sites while promoting sustainable cultural tourism.
about.teamSubtitle: A diverse group of professionals united by a shared passion for cultural preservation.

massawa.title: Heritage of Massawa
massawa.subtitle: Pearl of the Red Sea — A UNESCO World Heritage Tentative Site
massawa.introP1: Massawa, located on the Red Sea coast of Eritrea, is one of Africa's most historically significant port cities. For over two millennia, it has served as a vital trading hub connecting Africa, Arabia, and beyond.
massawa.introP2: The city's architecture reflects its rich multicultural heritage, featuring a unique blend of Ottoman, Egyptian, and Italian colonial styles built using locally quarried coral stone. The old town, spread across two islands connected by a causeway, contains some of the most remarkable historical structures in the Horn of Africa.
massawa.introP3: Despite damage during the Eritrean War of Independence, significant preservation efforts are underway to restore and protect this architectural treasure for future generations.

oldTown.title: Old Town (Massawa Island)
oldTown.description: The historic heart of Massawa featuring coral-stone buildings with Ottoman and Egyptian influences. Narrow winding streets lead to ancient mosques and traditional houses.

palace.title: Imperial Palace
palace.description: Once the winter residence of Ethiopian emperors, this grand structure showcases Italian colonial architecture blended with local design elements.

mosque.title: Sheikh Hanafi Mosque
mosque.description: One of the oldest mosques in Eritrea, featuring distinctive Ottoman architecture and beautiful coral stone carvings.

market.title: The Covered Market
market.description: A traditional covered bazaar that has served as the commercial heart of Massawa for centuries, still bustling with activity today.
